newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds more positive after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds more positive after Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rose about a quarter-point Tuesday afternoon following comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, traders and analysts said.
Greenspan's testimony before the Senate Budget Committee initially prompted a dip in Treasuries and mortgages, but both markets turned positive toward the end of the central banker's remarks.
"We've seen some good buying and no mortgage-banker selling whatsoever, so we've tightened up a couple of basis points," one trader said.
Analysts said the buying was broad-based, with some retail customers involved. By late on Tuesday, pass-throughs were up 3/32 to 9/32 overall.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 9/32 at 100-01/32, yielding 96 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 8/32 higher as well, at 99-29/32 and 100-02/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 10/32 at 99-30/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
In his testimony, Greenspan warned of tightness in the U.S. labor market but said job insecurity has kept wage inflation in check.
"The economy has retained considerable vigor, with few signs of the imbalances and inflationary tensions that have disrupted past expansions," he said.
The Fed chief's comments largely assuaged market fears of an interest rate hike at the February 4-5 policy meeting, Treasury analysts said.
